content.chs: # 目标 本文记录【未来之光】的目标体系与长期愿景。 ## 主要目标：引导人类进化 【未来之光】的主要目标是引导人类进化。在保障人类长期存续与繁衍的基础上，推动人类感知、认知、交流与存在方式的发展，使人类能够持续拓展自身的能力与可能性。 ## 终极目标：升维 本项目将人类进化的终极目标定义为“升维”，主要包括**信息升维**与**物理升维**。这两条方向处于不同的探索阶段，其具体含义、可行条件和实现方式需要分别研究。 ## 信息升维 信息升维的目标，是持续提高人类世界中信息组织、传递、感知和思考的维度。这里的维度首先用于描述信息的组织与呈现形式，以及人类处理这些信息的方式。 ### 从线性语言到多维交流 当前语言的常见传递形式是按词语或词元顺序展开的线性序列。本项目希望探索二维、三维乃至更高维的信息表达与交流方式，使信息能够通过空间关系、并行结构及其他多维组织方式呈现。 这一方向需要同时研究信息如何编码、如何传入、如何被理解，以及交流双方如何形成共同的认知基础。 ### 从感官输入到更高维思考 以视觉为例，本项目希望从现有的二维感光输入与大脑中的三维空间重建，进一步探索直接组织和接入三维信息的方式，并在此基础上发展更高维度的思考能力。人类已经能够借助空间与时间进行思考；项目希望继续拓展这一能力的边界。 声音所依托的机械波，以及光等电磁波，也属于这一探索范围。这些载体具有时间、空间、频率、振幅等多种可描述属性。项目关注如何利用这些属性组织和传递多维信息，以及人类如何感知与处理它们。 ### 灵魂的多维化 在长期愿景中，项目也将人类自身“灵魂”的多维化纳入探索范围。这一表述的具体含义、可观察现象及研究方式留待后续讨论，目前不预设实现机制。 ## 物理升维 物理升维是更远期的方向。项目认为，当前讨论其具体目标和实施方案仍过于超前，需要等待科学技术发展到足以支持相关研究的水平。 现阶段保留这一方向，不制定具体实施方案；未来再依据科学发现与技术能力，逐步讨论其含义、目标与可行路径。 ## 过渡目标：通往终极目标的步骤与基础 在本项目的目标体系中，财富、情感、艺术创作、科学进步、人口数量、教育程度、星空探索与征服，以及其他社会发展事项，都属于通向升维的**过渡目标**。 这些过渡目标为人类的长期存续、繁衍和进化提供步骤与基础。它们的作用需要结合其对终极目标的贡献加以理解，并随着知识、技术和社会条件的变化持续审视。 ## 目标规划方式 ### 长期：随机发散与维度突破 本项目采用以下规划假设：处于较低维度的社会与科技体系，无法预先完整窥知物理空间或信息空间升维后的状态，因此无法事先确定一条通往终局的完整最优路径。 基于这一假设，项目将随机发散视为长期寻求维度突破的基本方式：持续保留不同方向的探索，通过多样化尝试接触现有知识与认知框架之外的可能性。长期规划需要为未知方向留下空间，避免所有探索过早收敛到同一条已知路径。 ### 中短期：贪心选择与快速探索 在中短期跨度上，项目提出结合贪心算法与整体设计，辅助快速探索和风险控制。 贪心算法用于在当前已知条件、可比较的候选方向及既定风险边界内，选择被评估为下一步最优的方向。每一步取得新结果后，重新评估并选择后续行动。这种局部选择依赖当时的知识与评价标准，不保证整条路径达到全局最优。 ### 整体设计：多个探索子集与风险控制 在整体设计层面，项目提出将人类群体强制划分为多个探索子集的构想，使不同子集能够沿不同方向发展，保留探索路径的多样性。 这一设计有两个主要目的：一是避免持续沿单一评价方向优化，使整个社会过度收敛于局部最优；二是控制探索与扩张的范围，降低某一路径的失败扩散为人类世界整体毁灭的风险。这里以“过度梯度下降”比喻前一种收敛问题，具体风险能否被隔离仍需根据实际条件验证。 整体设计负责维持多条探索路径及其风险边界，贪心选择负责各阶段的下一步方向，随机发散则持续引入新的可能路径。三者需要配合使用。 ### 动态调整：随科技能力与终局认知修订 这一设计并非一成不变。随着人类掌握的科学技术能力、对终局的知识以及对风险的理解发生变化，项目需要重新审视探索子集的划分、方向配置、局部评价标准、扩张边界，以及随机发散与局部优化之间的比例。 这里的“终局知识”指当时能够获得的、关于最终目标及其实现条件的认识。每个阶段的设计都以当时的知识为依据，并为后续调整保留空间。 ## 短期目标与方案（10—100年） 相对于升维这一长期方向，本项目将规划启动后的10—100年视为短期探索窗口。在这一窗口内，重点推进人类生理结构、人类社会结构与生存空间三方面的发展。以下是研究与探索方案，各阶段根据证据、技术能力和实际风险动态调整。 ### 目标一：进化人类生理结构 推动人类生理结构的演化，使情感机制与大脑思维方式更容易理解、接纳并参与计划型社会，增强长期思考、复杂协作与共同规划的能力。 **出发点：** 本项目认为，人类的生理结构形成于漫长的进化历程，与地球环境及远古时期的生存竞争密切相关。情感、动机与奖励机制中保留着适应资源稀缺、环境威胁和繁衍压力的特征。 项目据此提出，既有生理机制与现代社会的发展要求、长期协作需求以及【未来之光】的终极目标之间存在需要研究的适应性差距。因此，目标一将对人体自身机制的研究与改造纳入长期方向，重点关注大脑结构、激素分泌、衰退与老化、遗传迭代四个方面。 **研究与改造方向：** - **大脑结构与思维机制：**研究脑结构、神经网络组织与感知、学习、情感、长期规划之间的关系，探索支持复杂协作及多维信息处理的能力发展方向。 - **激素分泌与生理调节：**研究内分泌系统与压力反应、情感体验、动机和奖励机制之间的关系，探索提升适应能力与生理稳定性的可能路径。 - **衰退与老化：**研究身体与认知功能随年龄变化的机制，探索延长健康寿命、维持学习能力与长期参与社会活动能力的方向。 - **遗传迭代：**研究遗传变异、代际传递与环境适应的关系，评估可能的改造方向是否具有可遗传性，以及其跨代影响与不确定性。 **探索方案：** - 研究情感、认知、生理条件与社会协作之间的关系，明确影响长期规划、信任、冲突处理和集体决策的因素。 - 先通过教育、协作环境和辅助工具探索认知适应性，再依据研究证据评估生理层面的可行方向；涉及人体的研究以知情自愿、健康保障和独立审查为前提。 - 以健康、认知能力、情感体验、个体自主性及长期协作效果共同评价研究结果，保留持续跟踪、退出与纠错机制。 ### 目标二：优化人类社会结构 突破资本主义市场在资源配置、长期投入与公共目标协调方面的限制，探索能够支持人类长期进化的计划型社会及其他社会组织形式。 **出发点与分析框架：** 本项目提出以下分析假设，并以优化算法作为理解社会运行的类比：在以贪婪和短视为重要约束的人类行为条件下，资本主义市场可以被视为对这些条件的最优适配解。它能够利用个体利益动机组织生产与交换，但其运行方向也持续受到这些动机的限制。 在这一框架中，市场依据局部收益与反馈不断调整的过程，被类比为“梯度下降”。项目认为，这种运行方式容易锁定在局部最优，也可能围绕某一极端方向出现过度扩张或发散，进而带来社会停滞、系统失衡乃至毁灭性冲突的风险。 **复杂度扩张及其局限：** 项目将现有市场应对上述问题的一种方式概括为“增加复杂度”：通过更多层次的制度、组织、产品与关系，增加可探索的方向。这被类比为提高算法搜索空间的维度，意在减少社会被单一路径和局部最优锁定的可能性。 与此同时，复杂度的增加也会提高社会的信息处理、协调与运行成本。按照本项目的判断，个体逐利及既有利益结构还可能压缩整体调整的有效幅度，即类比中的“步长变小”。当系统更加复杂而有效调整越来越缓慢时，继续增加复杂度的方案可能在未来触及自身无法解决的瓶颈。 **AI 与目标一的协同：** 项目希望利用 AI 的信息处理、长期推演与协调能力，减少贪婪和短视对资源配置及公共决策的影响，并降低复杂社会的协调成本。AI 的引入需要与长期目标、评价方式和制度设计共同推进，其实际效果通过研究与试点检验。 这一方向与目标一相互配合：目标一研究人类情感、奖励与思维机制的适应性变化，目标二研究相应的社会组织、激励与资源配置机制。项目希望通过人的能力与社会结构的共同演进，逐步优化人类社会的运行模式。 **探索方案：** - 建立可比较的社会与资源配置模型，研究市场、公共规划及不同组合方式在长期科研、基本生活保障、教育和基础设施上的表现。 - 在模型中比较制度复杂度、协调成本、调整速度、路径锁定和长期风险之间的关系，检验上述算法类比能够解释哪些现象及其适用边界。 - 评估 AI 辅助长期规划、信息整合与资源协调的效果，并结合目标一的研究进度调整社会模型与激励设计。 - 从模拟和局部、自愿参与的试点开始，探索公共资源配置、协作生产与长期规划机制，保留多个方案并行比较。 - 持续评估资源效率、生活质量、创新能力、分配结果、参与者权利与系统韧性，依据实际结果调整制度设计与扩展范围。 ### 目标三：扩展空间，建立多星球文明与独立探索体系 逐步推进太空殖民，将人类的生存、生产与知识积累扩展到多个星球及空间居住设施。在具备条件后，形成能够相对独立运行、彼此交流又保留不同发展方向的文明节点，为人类长期存续和升维探索提供更广阔的基础。 **出发点：从单一生存环境走向多种发展路径。** 本项目认为，人类长期集中于同一星球、共享高度关联的资源与制度体系，会使不同探索方向受到共同约束，也使人类整体暴露于某些共同风险。空间扩展的意义，在于增加可持续的生存空间，并为不同环境、技术路线与社会组织方式提供并行发展的条件。 目标三将前文的“多个探索子集”落实为空间发展的长期方向。不同星球的探索群体可以在各自环境中形成不同的知识、经验与组织方式，持续产生新的路径，为文明整体提供比较、学习和调整的机会。 **独立探索：保持多样性，积累可比较的经验。** 各文明节点可依据当地条件，探索不同的资源配置、生产协作、教育、科研与 AI 辅助治理模式。试点需要明确目标、适用条件、观察指标与调整方式，并记录成功、失败及意外结果。涉及居民参与的研究须建立知情、自愿参与及退出机制。 节点之间保留知识交流、公共研究记录与必要的互助机制。各节点在吸收其他节点成果时，需要检验其对自身环境的适用性，并维持继续探索不同路径的能力。 **自主生存：从地球补给走向本地维持。** 空间扩展应以生存能力逐步成熟为基础，推进运输、能源、生命保障、食物生产、资源循环、医疗、设备维修与制造等能力的发展。早期设施可以依赖地球支持；后续定居点需要逐步提高本地资源利用、关键设备维护和应对补给中断的能力。 地球继续承担重要的生态、人口与知识基础功能。空间扩展过程中，应持续维护地球及已有定居点的生存条件，使新增节点能够扩大文明的整体承载能力。 **风险控制：验证实际独立性。** 各节点的独立程度，需要依据能源、物资、生产、数据、治理与 AI 系统的实际依赖关系评估。空间距离之外，还需关注共享基础设施、同一技术缺陷或同一决策机制可能造成的关联失效。 扩张规模应与已验证的生命保障、维修、救援和风险处置能力相匹配。对尚未形成充分认识的环境与技术，先通过观测、模拟和无人设施积累证据，再评估长期有人居住的条件。 **与目标一、目标二的协同：** 目标一为不同生存环境下的人体健康、认知与适应能力提供研究基础；目标二为长期定居和群体协作提供社会组织与资源配置方案；目标三则为这两类研究提供多样化环境与独立探索空间。三者通过观测结果相互修订，共同服务于人类长期进化。 **探索方案：** - **基础能力建设：**研究空间运输、能源、资源循环和长期居住体系，并通过地面模拟、无人设施与轨道设施检验关键能力。 - **有限定居验证：**在满足条件的地点建立规模受控的居住与科研节点，持续评估健康、维护、资源保障及社会协作状况。 - **提高节点自主性：**逐步完善当地生产、维修、医疗与知识保存能力，减少关键环节对单一外部来源的依赖。 - **跨星球并行探索：**待不同星球具备长期定居条件后，开展相对独立的发展试点，通过共享记录比较不同路径的适用性与长期结果。 - **持续评价与调整：**以健康与生活质量、资源循环能力、补给中断承受时间、关键系统可维护性、知识积累和关联风险作为评价依据，决定扩展、修订或暂停。 ### 阶段安排 | 规划窗口 | 主要工作 | 阶段产出 | | --- | --- | --- | | 10—30年 | 建立基础研究、社会模拟与空间生存技术研究体系。 | 可复核的研究记录、评价标准与候选方案。 | | 30—60年 | 对满足条件的方向开展有限试点与技术验证。 | 可比较的试点结果、失败记录和修订后的设计。 | | 60—100年 | 依据已验证能力扩大成熟方案，并评估跨星球独立探索的条件。 | 可持续运行的探索体系，以及继续扩展、调整或暂停的依据。 | 各阶段以科学证据、参与条件、生存保障和风险控制能力作为推进依据。三个目标可以并行探索，具体进度与相互依赖关系随技术和知识的发展持续修订。 本文涉及的愿景不构成概念字典的新增条目。概念字典继续遵循其独立、严格的收录规则。
content.eng: # Goals This document records the goals and long-term vision of **Light of the Future**. ## Primary goal: guide human evolution The primary goal of Light of the Future is to guide human evolution. Building on humanity's long-term survival and reproduction, it seeks to advance human perception, cognition, communication, and modes of existence, enabling humanity to continually expand its capabilities and possibilities. ## Ultimate goal: dimensional advancement The project defines the ultimate goal of human evolution as “dimensional advancement,” encompassing **informational dimensional advancement** and **physical dimensional advancement**. These directions are at different stages of exploration; their meanings, enabling conditions, and potential methods require separate study. ## Informational dimensional advancement This direction aims to continually increase the dimensionality of how information is organized, transmitted, perceived, and thought about in the human world. Here, dimensionality initially refers to the organization and presentation of information and the ways humans process it. ### From linear language to multidimensional communication A common form of language transmission today is a linear sequence of words or tokens. The project seeks to explore two-dimensional, three-dimensional, and higher-dimensional forms of expression and communication, presenting information through spatial relationships, parallel structures, and other multidimensional arrangements. This requires studying how information is encoded, delivered, and understood, and how participants establish a shared cognitive basis for communication. ### From sensory input to higher-dimensional thought For vision, the project seeks to explore ways of directly organizing and receiving three-dimensional information beyond existing two-dimensional retinal input and the brain's reconstruction of three-dimensional space. It envisions using this as a basis for higher-dimensional thought. Humans already reason through space and time; the project seeks to further expand this capacity. Mechanical waves carrying sound and electromagnetic waves such as light are also within this scope. These carriers have multiple describable properties, including time, space, frequency, and amplitude. The project explores how these properties could organize and transmit multidimensional information, and how humans could perceive and process it. ### Multidimensionality of the soul The long-term vision also includes exploring multidimensionality of the human “soul.” The meaning of this expression, associated observable phenomena, and methods of study remain topics for future discussion. No implementation mechanism is presumed at this stage. ## Physical dimensional advancement Physical dimensional advancement is a more distant direction. The project considers it premature to formulate concrete objectives or implementation plans before science and technology have progressed enough to support the relevant research. For now, this direction is retained without a concrete implementation plan. Its meaning, objectives, and possible paths will be considered as scientific discoveries and technical capabilities develop. ## Transitional goals: steps and foundations toward the ultimate goal Within the project's goal hierarchy, wealth, emotion, artistic creation, scientific progress, population size, educational attainment, exploration and conquest of the stars, and other aspects of social development are **transitional goals** on the path to dimensional advancement. These transitional goals provide steps and foundations for humanity's long-term survival, reproduction, and evolution. Their roles should be understood in relation to their contribution to the ultimate goal and continually reassessed as knowledge, technology, and social conditions change. ## Goal-planning approach ### Long term: random exploration and dimensional breakthroughs The project adopts the following planning assumption: societies and technologies operating at lower dimensional levels cannot fully anticipate the state that would follow dimensional advancement in physical or informational space. A complete optimal path to the ultimate outcome therefore cannot be determined in advance. On this assumption, the project treats random, divergent exploration as the fundamental long-term approach to dimensional breakthroughs: maintain exploration in different directions and use diverse attempts to encounter possibilities beyond existing knowledge and cognitive frameworks. Long-term planning must leave room for unknown directions and avoid premature convergence of all exploration onto one known path. ### Short and medium term: greedy selection and rapid exploration Over short and medium horizons, the project proposes combining greedy algorithms with overall design to support rapid exploration and risk control. Greedy selection chooses the direction assessed as best for the next step, given currently known conditions, comparable candidate directions, and established risk boundaries. After each step produces new results, subsequent actions are reassessed. These local choices depend on the knowledge and evaluation criteria available at the time and do not guarantee a globally optimal path. ### Overall design: multiple exploration subsets and risk control At the level of overall design, the project proposes a compulsory division of humanity into multiple exploration subsets, allowing different subsets to develop in different directions and preserve a diversity of exploratory paths. This design has two main purposes: to prevent repeated optimization against a single criterion from driving society into a local optimum, and to limit exploration and expansion so that failure along one path is less likely to spread into the destruction of the human world as a whole. “Excessive gradient descent” is used here as an analogy for the first convergence problem. Whether risks can actually be contained requires validation under the relevant conditions. Overall design maintains multiple exploration paths and their risk boundaries; greedy selection determines the next direction at each stage; random exploration continually introduces new possible paths. The three approaches are intended to work together. ### Dynamic revision: adapt to scientific capabilities and knowledge of the ultimate outcome The design is not fixed. As humanity's scientific and technical capabilities, knowledge of the ultimate outcome, and understanding of risks change, the project must reassess the division of exploration subsets, the allocation of directions, local evaluation criteria, expansion boundaries, and the balance between random exploration and local optimization. “Knowledge of the ultimate outcome” means the understanding available at a given time of the final objective and the conditions for achieving it. Each stage of design rests on the knowledge then available and leaves room for subsequent revision. ## Short-term goals and approaches (10–100 years) Relative to the long-term direction of dimensional advancement, the project treats years 10–100 after the planning effort begins as a short-term exploration window. Work in this window focuses on human physiology, social structures, and the space available for human habitation. The following research and exploration approaches are subject to revision based on evidence, technical capabilities, and actual risks. ### Goal one: evolve human physiology Advance human physiological evolution so that emotional mechanisms and patterns of thought can more readily understand, accept, and participate in a planned society, strengthening long-term thinking, complex cooperation, and shared planning. **Rationale:** The project takes the view that human physiology developed through a long evolutionary history closely connected to Earth's environment and ancient survival competition. Emotional, motivational, and reward mechanisms retain characteristics associated with adaptation to scarce resources, environmental threats, and reproductive pressures. On this basis, the project proposes that there are adaptive gaps to investigate between existing physiological mechanisms, the demands of modern society and long-term cooperation, and the ultimate goals of Light of the Future. Goal one therefore includes research into and modification of human biological mechanisms as a long-term direction, focusing on brain structure, hormone secretion, decline and aging, and genetic change across generations. **Research and modification directions:** - **Brain structure and thought processes:** study relationships between brain structure, neural-network organization, perception, learning, emotion, and long-term planning, exploring the development of capabilities for complex cooperation and multidimensional information processing. - **Hormone secretion and physiological regulation:** study relationships between the endocrine system, stress responses, emotional experience, motivation, and reward mechanisms, exploring possible paths toward greater adaptability and physiological stability. - **Decline and aging:** study mechanisms of age-related changes in physical and cognitive functions, exploring ways to extend healthy lifespan and sustain learning and long-term participation in society. - **Genetic change across generations:** study relationships between genetic variation, transmission across generations, and environmental adaptation, assessing whether possible modifications would be heritable and examining their effects and uncertainties across generations. **Exploration approach:** - Study relationships between emotion, cognition, physiological conditions, and social cooperation, identifying factors affecting long-term planning, trust, conflict resolution, and collective decisions. - Begin by exploring cognitive adaptability through education, cooperative environments, and assistive tools, then assess possible physiological directions based on research evidence. Human-subject research requires informed, voluntary participation, health protections, and independent review. - Evaluate outcomes through health, cognitive capabilities, emotional experience, individual autonomy, and sustained cooperation, with provisions for ongoing follow-up, withdrawal, and correction. ### Goal two: optimize human social structures Move beyond the limitations of capitalist markets in resource allocation, long-term investment, and coordination of public objectives. Explore planned societies and other forms of social organization that could support humanity's long-term evolution. **Rationale and analytical framework:** The project proposes the following analytical assumptions, using optimization algorithms as an analogy for social processes: under conditions where greed and short-term thinking are significant constraints on human behavior, capitalist markets can be regarded as the best-fitting solution to those conditions. They organize production and exchange through individual incentives, while remaining constrained by those incentives. Within this framework, a market's repeated adjustments in response to local returns and feedback are likened to “gradient descent.” The project argues that this process can become locked into local optima or expand excessively along an extreme direction, creating risks of social stagnation, systemic imbalance, and potentially destructive conflict. **Increasing complexity and its limits:** The project characterizes one market response to these problems as “increasing complexity”: adding layers of institutions, organizations, products, and relationships to create more directions for exploration. This is likened to increasing the dimensionality of an algorithm's search space, with the intention of reducing the likelihood of society becoming locked into one path or a local optimum. At the same time, greater complexity raises the costs of information processing, coordination, and social operation. In the project's assessment, individual pursuit of advantage and established interests may also reduce the effective scale of collective adjustment—the analogy's “smaller step size.” As systems become more complex while effective adjustment slows, further increases in complexity may eventually encounter bottlenecks this approach cannot resolve. **Coordination between AI and goal one:** The project seeks to use AI's information-processing, long-horizon analysis, and coordination capabilities to reduce the influence of greed and short-term thinking on resource allocation and public decisions, while lowering the coordination costs of a complex society. AI adoption must develop alongside long-term objectives, evaluation methods, and institutional design, with its effects assessed through research and pilots. This direction complements goal one: goal one studies adaptive changes in human emotion, reward, and thought processes, while goal two studies corresponding forms of social organization, incentives, and resource allocation. The project seeks to progressively improve society's operation through the joint development of human capabilities and social structures. **Exploration approach:** - Develop comparable models of society and resource allocation to examine markets, public planning, and combinations of the two in long-term research, basic living provision, education, and infrastructure. - Compare institutional complexity, coordination costs, adjustment speed, path dependence, and long-term risk within these models, testing which phenomena the algorithmic analogy can explain and where its applicability ends. - Evaluate AI-assisted long-term planning, information integration, and resource coordination, adapting social models and incentive designs as research under goal one progresses. - Begin with simulations and limited, voluntary pilots of public resource allocation, cooperative production, and long-term planning, retaining multiple approaches for parallel comparison. - Continually assess resource efficiency, quality of life, innovation, distributional outcomes, participants' rights, and systemic resilience. Revise institutional designs and the scope of expansion based on observed results. ### Goal three: expand into space and establish a multiplanetary civilization with independent exploration Progressively advance space colonization, extending human habitation, production, and knowledge accumulation across multiple planets and space habitats. When conditions permit, establish relatively autonomous centers of civilization that exchange knowledge while retaining distinct development paths, broadening the foundations for humanity's long-term survival and exploration of dimensional advancement. **Rationale: from a single living environment to multiple development paths.** The project takes the view that humanity's concentration on one planet, sharing highly interconnected resource and institutional systems, places common constraints on exploration and exposes humanity to certain shared risks. Expansion into space aims to increase sustainable living space and enable parallel development across different environments, technological approaches, and forms of social organization. Goal three translates the earlier concept of “multiple exploration subsets” into a long-term direction for spatial development. Communities on different planets could develop distinct knowledge, experience, and organizational forms in their respective environments, continually producing new paths for civilization to compare, learn from, and adapt. **Independent exploration: preserve diversity and accumulate comparable experience.** Each center could explore resource allocation, cooperative production, education, research, and AI-assisted governance suited to local conditions. Pilots should specify objectives, applicable conditions, observation criteria, and revision procedures, recording successes, failures, and unexpected outcomes. Research involving residents requires informed, voluntary participation and provisions for withdrawal. Centers retain knowledge exchange, shared research records, and necessary mutual assistance. When adopting results from elsewhere, each center should assess their applicability to its own environment while preserving its ability to explore different paths. **Autonomous survival: from Earth-based supply to local sustainment.** Expansion should follow the gradual maturation of survival capabilities, including transportation, energy, life support, food production, resource recycling, healthcare, equipment repair, and manufacturing. Early facilities may rely on support from Earth; later settlements should progressively improve local resource use, critical equipment maintenance, and resilience to supply interruptions. Earth continues to provide essential ecological, population, and knowledge foundations. Expansion should maintain living conditions on Earth and at existing settlements so that new centers increase civilization's overall capacity to support life. **Risk control: verify actual independence.** The autonomy of each center must be assessed through its actual dependencies in energy, materials, production, data, governance, and AI systems. Beyond physical distance, assessments must consider correlated failures caused by shared infrastructure, common technical defects, or shared decision-making mechanisms. The scale of expansion should match demonstrated capabilities in life support, maintenance, rescue, and risk response. For environments and technologies that remain insufficiently understood, accumulate evidence through observation, simulation, and uncrewed facilities before assessing conditions for long-term human habitation. **Coordination with goals one and two:** Goal one provides a research foundation for human health, cognition, and adaptation in different living environments. Goal two provides approaches to social organization and resource allocation for long-term settlement and cooperation. Goal three supplies diverse environments and independent exploration spaces for both. Observations inform revisions across all three goals in support of humanity's long-term evolution. **Exploration approach:** - **Build foundational capabilities:** research transportation, energy, resource recycling, and long-term habitation, testing critical capabilities through ground simulations, uncrewed facilities, and orbital infrastructure. - **Validate limited settlements:** establish habitation and research centers of controlled scale where prerequisites are met, continually assessing health, maintenance, resource provision, and social cooperation. - **Increase local autonomy:** progressively develop local production, repair, healthcare, and knowledge preservation, reducing reliance on a single external source for critical functions. - **Explore different planets in parallel:** once conditions support long-term settlement on different planets, conduct relatively independent development pilots and use shared records to compare the applicability and long-term outcomes of different paths. - **Evaluate and revise continually:** base expansion, revision, or suspension on health and quality of life, resource-recycling capabilities, endurance during supply interruptions, maintainability of critical systems, accumulated knowledge, and correlated risks. ### Phasing | Planning window | Main work | Expected outputs | | --- | --- | --- | | Years 10–30 | Establish foundational research, social simulations, and research into space-habitation technologies. | Reviewable research records, evaluation criteria, and candidate approaches. | | Years 30–60 | Conduct limited pilots and technical validation where the prerequisites are met. | Comparable pilot outcomes, records of failures, and revised designs. | | Years 60–100 | Expand mature approaches based on demonstrated capabilities and assess conditions for independent exploration on different planets. | Sustainable exploratory systems and evidence supporting further expansion, revision, or suspension. | Progress at each stage depends on scientific evidence, conditions for participation, survival provisions, and risk-control capabilities. The three goals may be explored in parallel, with their pace and dependencies continually revised as technology and knowledge develop.
